reason: E1 demonstrates that coherent nanoprecipitates in a W-based RHEA improve strength and ductility, supporting the dislocation transmission premise, but it does not address irradiation or defect sink behavior. E3 shows phase stability under annealing and irradiation of as-sintered RHEAs but does not involve controlled precipitation or coherent interfaces. No cited evidence supports the key premises that annealing induces uniformly dispersed coherent precipitates, that these precipitates act as efficient defect sinks, or that they reduce void swelling under irradiation.
premises: Coherent nanoprecipitates can be induced in W-based RHEAs via post-sintering annealing
Coherent interfaces facilitate dislocation transmission and relieve stress concentrations
Nanoscale coherent precipitates act as efficient defect sinks, enhancing vacancy-interstitial recombination
The proposed annealing yields uniformly dispersed nanoscale coherent precipitates
Reduced void swelling and retained mechanical properties are achievable under fusion-relevant irradiation
